title: Col. John Holder at Lower Howard's Creek
summary: John Holder (1753–1799) came to Kentucky in 1777, commanded Fort Boonesborough in 1779, and in 1782 planted Holder's Station near Lower Howard's Creek.
bodyMarkdown:
[John Holder](/people/#john-holder) (1753–1799) came to Kentucky in 1777, during the hardest years of the Revolution on the frontier. He served under [George Rogers Clark](/people/#george-rogers-clark) and in 1779 commanded the garrison at Fort Boonesborough, the Kentucky River settlement founded by [Daniel Boone](/people/#daniel-boone).

He was tied to Boonesborough by marriage as well. His wife, [Fanny Callaway](/people/#fanny-callaway), was a daughter of [Col. Richard Callaway](/stories/col-richard-callaway-of-boonesborough/). In July 1776 she was one of the three girls captured with [Jemima Boone](/people/#jemima-boone) while canoeing on the river and rescued days later by Boone's party.

In 1782 Holder planted his own station about a mile downstream from Boonesborough, on the north bank of the Kentucky River near the mouth of Lower Howard's Creek, in what became Clark County. That year was one of the deadliest on the frontier, and a station was first of all a fort, a ring of cabins and stockade where families could hold out against raids.

As the danger eased, Holder's Station turned into a business center. Holder ran a store, a tavern, and a ferry across the river. He built a warehouse, a mill, and a boatyard. Farmers brought tobacco, flour, and other produce down to the landing, where flatboats were built and loaded for the long float to New Orleans. The creek valley became one of the earliest industrial corridors in the Bluegrass, lined over time with mills and stone buildings.

Holder also held public office. He served as a Clark County justice under Governor [Isaac Shelby](/people/#isaac-shelby). He died in 1799.

## Kentucky today

Kentucky Historical Marker 1048 remembers Holder. The Lower Howard's Creek Nature and Heritage Preserve in Clark County protects the creek valley, and the John Holder Trail leads past ruins of the old mills. Fort Boonesborough State Park, a short drive upriver, has a rebuilt fort.
Source: [Col. John Holder (ExploreKYHistory)](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/905)
